mainEntity.name: How many 80 lb bags make a cubic yard?

acceptedAnswer.text: An 80 lb bag yields about 0.60 cubic feet, so one cubic yard (27 ft³) needs about 45 bags. A 60 lb bag yields about 0.45 ft³ (60 bags per yard) and a 50 lb bag about 0.375 ft³ (72 bags per yard).

mainEntity.name: How much extra concrete should I order?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most people add 5% to 10%. Use more for rough or uneven subgrade, deep forms or long trenches. Running short mid-pour can cause a cold joint, which is a weak seam in the slab.

mainEntity.name: Should I use bags or a ready-mix truck?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bags suit small jobs such as post holes and small pads. Once a pour passes about a cubic yard, mixing by hand is slow and the mix can vary, so a truck is usually the better choice. Compare the totals above with your local quote.

mainEntity.name: How much does a cubic yard of concrete weigh?

acceptedAnswer.text: Normalweight concrete weighs about 145 to 150 pounds per cubic foot, so roughly 3,900 to 4,050 pounds per cubic yard. This tool uses 145 lb/ft³ for the weight estimate.

mainEntity.name: How thick should a concrete slab be?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 4 inch slab is common for patios and walkways. Driveways and garage floors are often 5 to 6 inches, and heavy loads need more. Confirm the thickness with your local building code or an engineer.

mainEntity.name: How many 80 lb bags of concrete are in a cubic yard?

acceptedAnswer.text: About 45, because a cubic yard is 27 ft³ and an 80 lb bag yields about 0.60 ft³. A 60 lb bag needs 60 and a 50 lb bag needs 72.

mainEntity.name: How many square feet does a cubic yard of concrete cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: At 4 inches thick, about 81 ft². At 6 inches it covers 54 ft². The formula is 324 ÷ thickness in inches, before any waste allowance.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate concrete for a slab?

acceptedAnswer.text: Length × width × thickness in feet ÷ 27 gives cubic yards. A 12 × 12 ft slab at 4 in is 144 × (4 ÷ 12) ÷ 27 = 1.78 yd³, or 1.96 yd³ with 10% waste.

mainEntity.name: How much concrete do I need for a 10 x 10 slab?

acceptedAnswer.text: At 4 inches, 1.23 yd³ with no waste, or 1.36 yd³ with a 10% allowance. At 6 inches it is 1.85 yd³, or 2.04 yd³ with 10% extra.

mainEntity.name: How many bags of concrete for a fence post hole?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 10 in wide, 30 in deep hole holds about 1.4 ft³, so about 3 bags of 80 lb mix. Larger or deeper holes need more.

mainEntity.name: How do I convert cubic metres to cubic yards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiply by 1.308. A 2.2 m³ pour is about 2.88 yd³. To go the other way multiply cubic yards by 0.7646.

mainEntity.name: How much does a cubic yard of concrete weigh?

acceptedAnswer.text: About 3,900 pounds using 145 lb per cubic foot (27 × 145 = 3,915 lb). The calculator uses this figure.

mainEntity.name: Does the calculator include gravel base or rebar?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It estimates the concrete only. Use the gravel calculator for the base, and check your plans for reinforcement.
